kurz: Economic and market data as of 19 September 2026, and a guide to keeping them up to date yourself.

bloecke.md:
All the figures in this lesson will be out of date after a while. They are as of 19 September 2026, and the underlying publications date from the period from 30 June to 18 September 2026. You do not need to memorise such a snapshot. It is useful because it shows which variables fit together, which contradict each other and where you need to look things up yourself once a quarter has passed.

Every figure comes with three pieces of information: the reference date, the publishing body and the revision behaviour, that is, how much the value is corrected afterwards. A daily yield from 18 September has already changed by 19 September. A GDP flash estimate is an estimate that can shift by several tenths in the second estimate. For the second quarter of 2026, Destatis (the Federal Statistical Office) reported +0.2% in the flash estimate of 30 July and +0.3% in the detailed results of 25 August. A debt ratio is a quarterly value that is published with a delay of around three months. Only with these three pieces of information can the values in a table be checked and compared; without them, they remain unsupported claims.

bloecke.titel: Key figures at a glance, as of 19 Sep 2026

bloecke.md:
## Supply shock and key interest rates

Taken together, the rows of the table form a pattern. Headline inflation has risen again in 2026, in Germany from 2.3% in June to 2.9% in August. [[Core inflation]], by contrast, has not risen. It stands at 2.4% in Germany, in the euro area and for the US CPI. The breakdown by product group shows the cause: German energy prices +10.5%, motor fuels +27.7%, food +0.1%. A barrel of Brent crude cost $109.51 on 9 September and $130.80 on 15 September.

Rising prices with weaker production are the typical pattern of a supply shock. Monetary policy cannot correct both at the same time. It can only prevent the shock from spreading to the core rate through wages and expectations. That is why the ECB and the Fed changed direction in 2026 and raised their key interest rates. The ECB raised the deposit facility rate to 2.25% with effect from 17 June and to 2.50% with effect from 16 September. On 16 September, the Fed decided unanimously to raise its target range to 3.75% to 4.00% with effect from 17 September, for the first time since 2023. The ECB projection of 10 September puts headline inflation for 2026, 2027 and 2028 at 3.0%, 2.5% and 2.1%, with growth of 0.9%, 1.4% and 1.5%. The inflation target will therefore be reached in 2028 at the earliest.

bloecke.titel: Headline and core inflation in the US, July 2025 to August 2026
bloecke.unter: From spring 2026, the headline rate rises with the energy price, while the core rate remains close to 2.5%.

bloecke.md:
## Long-term interest rates and leading indicators

Long-term interest rates have risen more than short-term ones. The yield on ten-year Bunds averaged 3.18% in August and stood at around 3.5% in mid-September, its highest level since 2011. The yield on ten-year US Treasuries reached 5.01% on 16 September, a level last seen in 2007. This contradicts the assumption that the central bank also controls long-term interest rates. For long maturities, the market prices in inflation and supply risks, regardless of what is decided at the eight policy meetings a year.

The [[yield curve]] has a normal shape. On 18 September, the spread between the ten-year and two-year yields was +0.25 percentage points, and between ten years and three months +0.87 percentage points. The Sahm indicator, at -0.07 percentage points in August, was also well below its trigger threshold of +0.50. These two series currently give no recession signal. That does not rule out a recession; it only means that the two most frequently cited leading indicators are not showing a warning at the moment.

bloecke.titel: US yield curve, calculated from the documented spreads
bloecke.unter: Illustrative calculation: the ten-year yield of 4.94% less the spreads of +0.25 (10y-2y) and +0.87 percentage points (10y-3m) gives 4.69% and 4.07%, that is, a flat but normally rising curve.

bloecke.md:
## Return after tax and inflation

In nominal terms, 2026 looks like a turn in the interest rate cycle. The yield on German bonds outstanding (Umlaufrendite) stands at around 3.5%; at the end of 2021 it was -0.28%. For purchasing power, however, what counts is that tax is levied on the nominal return and inflation is only deducted afterwards. Capital income is subject to [[flat-rate withholding tax (Abgeltungsteuer)]] of 25% under Section 32d(1) EStG (Income Tax Act), plus solidarity surcharge, 26.375% in total. With church tax, it is around 28%. The tax is only levied on income above the saver's allowance (Sparer-Pauschbetrag) of €1,000, or above €2,000 for joint assessment (Section 20(9) EStG). For small portfolios, this rule is the most important one in tax law.

bloecke.titel: Return on a 10-year Bund after tax and inflation
bloecke.unter: Illustrative calculation with a yield of 3.52% (18 Sep 2026), 26.375% flat-rate withholding tax and 2.9% inflation, without church tax and without the saver's allowance.

bloecke.md: Of a 3.52% yield, 2.59% remains after tax. With inflation at 2.9%, that gives around -0.3 percentage points in real terms. Interest rates on instant-access savings accounts follow the deposit facility rate of 2.50% at a distance and with a delay of several weeks. For instant-access savings, the result is therefore even more clearly negative. The statement “Finally, interest again” thus only holds in nominal terms.

The level of interest rates has an effect in two further places. Mortgage rates are based on the capital market, not on the key interest rate. They follow the yields on Pfandbriefe (German covered bonds) and Bunds and can therefore rise even when the ECB does not change its rates. In addition, the [[advance lump sum (Vorabpauschale)]] on accumulating funds rises with the level of interest rates. The base return (Basisertrag) is derived from 70% of a base interest rate (Basiszins), which the Deutsche Bundesbank calculates at the start of the year from the yield on long-term public-sector bonds and the Federal Ministry of Finance (BMF) publishes, under Section 18(1) and (4) InvStG (Investment Tax Act). For equity funds, the 30% partial exemption (Teilfreistellung) reduces the taxable amount (Section 20 InvStG). This must be distinguished from the basic rate of interest under Section 247 BGB (Civil Code), which has stood at 1.52% since 1 July 2026. It serves only as a reference figure for default interest. Default interest is 6.52% towards consumers and 10.52% in business transactions not involving consumers (Section 288 BGB).

## Valuation of the US stock market

Two valuation measures are available for the US stock market. The [[Shiller CAPE]] of the S&P 500 stood at 40.94 on 18 September 2026. For comparison, the historical mean is 17.42, the median 16.13 and the dotcom peak 44.19 in December 1999. The [[Buffett indicator]] stood at 244% as of 30 June 2026. It relates a market value of $78.10 trillion to annualised GDP of $32.06 trillion and is thus around 2.6 standard deviations above its long-term trend.

Neither measure is suitable for timing a purchase or sale. They correlate with returns over roughly the following ten years, but hardly with those of the next twelve months. From 2017 to 2026, the CAPE was almost continuously above 27. Investors who got out because of this were not invested for years. Both measures also have a design flaw. The Buffett indicator compares a market value that also contains profits earned worldwide with purely domestic GDP. As a result, the value rises over decades, and the comparison with the 1970s is distorted. In the case of the CAPE, today's US accounting rules depress reported earnings in crisis years more than in the past, because companies have to write down impaired goodwill and other losses in value immediately. In addition, companies today pay out a smaller share of their profits as dividends and buy back more of their own shares. As a result, earnings per share grow faster, and their ten-year average lags further behind current earnings. Both make the CAPE higher than it would be under earlier accounting rules and earlier payout practice.

For market concentration, that is, the weight of the largest companies in the index, the sources used here contain no documented value for September 2026. This figure can be found in the index provider's monthly factsheet or in the holdings list of an index ETF, where you can count it yourself in two minutes. A percentage quoted from memory would be undocumented and therefore does not belong in the overview.

bloecke.titel: Shiller CAPE of the S&P 500 in historical comparison
bloecke.unter: The current value is closer to the dotcom record than to the mean since 1881, which says something about expected ten-year returns, but nothing about the next quarter.

bloecke.md:
## Updating the table yourself

An overview like this has to be maintained regularly. Twenty minutes a month is enough if you proceed in the same order each time.

schritte.text: Save the sources as bookmarks instead of searching: Destatis for German prices and GDP, Eurostat for the euro area, the ECB and the Fed for key interest rates, the BLS for US prices and the labour market, FRED for yields, spreads and money supply. Data portals are convenient, but only show copies of the original data.

The US employment report is published on the first Friday of the month at 14:30 German time, US consumer prices in the middle of the month, the German inflation estimate at the end of the month and the GDP flash estimate around 30 days after the end of the quarter. The ECB and the Fed each hold eight interest rate meetings a year.
Every cell gets a date and a source. A yield without a date cannot be put into context.
If a value changes, the old one stays next to the new one. After a year, you can see which series are often revised, for example orders received and employment. Key interest rates are never revised.

Do not mix up gross debt and the Maastricht ratio, the annualised rate and the quarter-on-quarter rate, the German CPI and the HICP, or the US CPI and the PCE. A row without a verifiable origin should be deleted.

bloecke.titel: Sources of error in the table
bloecke.md:
- Depending on the measure, you get a different inflation rate. The German CPI stands at 2.9%, the euro area HICP at 3.2% (flash estimate 3.3%) and the US CPI at 3.4%. The US PCE price index was 3.4% in August, core PCE excluding food and energy 3.0%. The Fed measures its target by the headline PCE index, the ECB by the HICP. The wrong series gives a wrong deviation from target.
- Debt ratios are defined differently. The US ratio of 122.6% is federal debt including securities held by government trust funds. The values of 64.4% and 88.9% are Maastricht ratios for general government, made up of the federal government, the states (Länder), municipalities and social security. The 88.9% applies to the euro area of 21 countries; without Bulgaria it would be 89.4%.
- Sentiment surveys and production data can diverge. The German manufacturing PMI stood at 54.3 in August 2026, its highest level since May 2022, while industrial production in July was -1.8% year on year according to revised figures. Both figures are correct, but they measure different things.
- Daily values become outdated within a few hours. Oil, yields and exchange rates in the table are reference-date values from 11 to 18 September 2026. The Brent price alone changed by just over $21 between 9 and 15 September.

A snapshot is not a forecast. The finding “valuation high, real after-tax interest rate negative, core rate stable” does not produce a buy or sell signal. It helps you estimate which returns can be expected in the long run and how much purchasing power money held without interest loses.

- The Bund yield of 3.52% is the Bundesbank's daily value derived from the term structure for 18 September and changes every day. The monthly average for August 2026 is 3.18%.
- The Buffett indicator is a quarterly value as of 30 June 2026. The September level is likely to differ.
- For the euro area HICP in August 2026, the flash estimate of 1 September gave 3.3% (as did the ECB press conference), and the final result of 17 September gave 3.2%.
- German GDP for the second quarter of 2026 is +0.2% or +0.3%, depending on the publication. The third estimate of 30 September raised US GDP growth for the same quarter from 1.5% to 2.2% annualised.
- Several PMI values come from secondary sources, because the providers only make their original reports available after registration.

Such ranges are normal. The figures nevertheless remain usable if you know the ranges and phrase your statements with corresponding caution.

mitnehmen: Every macro figure comes with a reference date, a source and an indication of how much it is revised.

In August 2026, headline inflation rose because of energy prices, while the core rates in Germany, the euro area and for the US CPI stood at 2.4%, which points to a supply shock rather than a demand boom.
For German savers, tax is deducted before inflation, so a Bund yield of 3.52% gives around -0.3 percentage points in real terms after 26.375% flat-rate withholding tax and 2.9% inflation.
A CAPE of 40.9 and a Buffett indicator of 244% point to lower expected returns over the next ten years, but say hardly anything about the next twelve months.
A table you maintain yourself shows when the situation changes, without you having to rely on forecasts.

begriffe.text: Nominal interest rate less capital income withholding tax (Kapitalertragsteuer) and less inflation. For German investors, it is the only meaningful figure, because the tax is deducted before inflation. In this way, a Bund yield of 3.52% (18 September 2026) with inflation of 2.9% (August 2026) turns into around -0.3 percentage points of purchasing power.

begriffe.begriff: Basic rate of interest under Section 247 BGB
begriffe.text: A reference figure that the Bundesbank updates every six months and that has stood at 1.52% since 1 July 2026. It is neither an investment rate nor a lending rate and serves as the reference for default interest under Section 288 BGB (plus 5 or 9 percentage points respectively). It must be distinguished from the base interest rate (Basiszins) for the advance lump sum under Section 18 InvStG.
Subsequent correction of a published statistic. GDP, employment and industrial production are revised regularly, sometimes considerably. The first release is an estimate and not a measured value.

Quarterly change extrapolated to a full year, the standard for GDP in the US. An annualised rate of 1.5% corresponds to around 0.37% growth over the previous quarter, the presentation customary in Europe.
